sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Apache County, Arizona?
sections.html:
Deeds for Apache County property are recorded at the County Recorder's office in St. Johns, the county seat. The Recorder's page lists the office at 75 West Cleveland, PO Box 425, St. Johns, AZ 85936, with the phone at 928-337-7515 and the fax at 928-337-7676.

ItemWhat the county lists
Office hours6:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through Thursday
Recording questions928-337-7515, recordings@co.apache.az.us
County RecorderLarry Noble
Records go back to1879

The county says every recorded document is treated as an original, and the office preserves and indexes the records and lets the public view them. Because the counter is open four days a week, plan a closing around Monday to Thursday if you ever need to record in person.

sections.h2: What does the Apache County Recorder do besides recording deeds?
sections.html:
The Recorder preserves and indexes documents and also runs voter registration and early ballots for the county. For a seller, the document side is what matters.

The Recorder's page lists several recording resources worth knowing before you submit anything:

  • A recording cover sheet.
  • A page on recording requirements under A.R.S. 11-480.
  • A form for setting up an account with the office.
  • A blank affidavit of property value.
  • A page on homestead exemptions and one on recordings and property transfers.
  • A search tool for viewing recorded documents.

Most sales are recorded by a title or escrow company on the seller's behalf, so many owners never visit the counter. If you are handling an inherited or family transfer without a title company, call the office first and ask what it needs.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Apache County?
sections.html:
State law sets the base fee at $30 per instrument for most recorded papers. The figures below come from A.R.S. 11-475, which governs county recorder fees.

ServiceFee under A.R.S. 11-475
Recording most papers required or authorized by law$30 per instrument
Recording for the U.S., the state or a political subdivision at its own request$15 per instrument
Copies of a record$1 per page or partial page
Recorder's certificate and seal on a copy$3 extra

The statute notes that those recording fees already include an amount charged under another section, 11-475.01. Apache County's own page may list different copy pricing or add other charges, so confirm with the office before you send a check.

sections.h2: What is the affidavit of property value, and when is it needed?
sections.html:
Arizona requires an affidavit of legal value, which the Recorder's page calls the affidavit of property value, to be attached to a deed or sales contract when it is recorded. Under A.R.S. 11-1133, both buyer and seller, or an agent for either, certify the details on a form approved by the Department of Revenue.

The affidavit asks for a lot of information.

  • Names, mailing addresses and phone numbers of the buyer and seller.
  • The address where a tax statement may be sent.
  • The full legal description and the situs address, if any.
  • The date of sale and the total price paid, with any cash down payment and the type of financing.
  • Whether personal property worth 5% or more of the price changed hands.
  • The assessor's parcel number, the conditions of the deal, and whether a home will be owner-occupied or rented.

The recorder must refuse to record a deed or sales contract if the affidavit is incomplete, unless the instrument carries a notation of an exemption under A.R.S. 11-1134. An affidavit counts as complete when each item is answered or marked not applicable.

sections.h2: Which Apache County deeds skip the affidavit?
sections.html:
Several transfers are exempt, and the deed itself must name the exemption on its face when it is recorded. A.R.S. 11-1134 lists them.

Exempt instruments include:

  • A deed of gift, and a quitclaim deed made for no money to quiet title.
  • A conveyance made under a court order.
  • A trustee's deed under a deed of trust power of sale, and transfers that only release or give security for a debt.
  • A deed that confirms or corrects an earlier recorded deed.
  • A transfer for nominal consideration between spouses, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, or siblings, for residential property.
  • A transfer to or from a trustee or trust beneficiary for nominal consideration, and a transfer under a beneficiary deed for nominal consideration.
  • A deed for a sale for delinquent taxes, and a transfer on partition.

Most arm's-length sales are not on this list, so a normal cash sale to a buyer needs the completed affidavit. If you are not sure which side your deed falls on, ask an Arizona title company or attorney.

sections.h2: How does the Treasurer's role as public trustee connect to recording?
sections.html:
In Apache County the Treasurer serves as the public trustee, so deeds of trust name the Treasurer as trustee. The Treasurer's page says the office may make trustee sales, issue certificates of purchase and redemption, issue trustee's deeds and release deeds of trust when the lender asks.

That matters when you sell a house with a loan. Once the loan is paid off at closing, the lender requests a release, and the release is recorded with the Recorder. An unreleased deed of trust can hold up the next sale of the property, so confirm that your payoff produced a recorded release.

The Treasurer's office is in the same building as the Recorder, at 75 West Cleveland in St. Johns, and keeps the same Monday to Thursday hours.

sections.h2: What is Apache County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Apache County is a large, rural county in the northeast corner of Arizona. It was organized in 1879, covers 11,218 square miles, and is the third-largest county in the state by area. The county seat is St. Johns, and the largest town is Eagar.

A large share of the land is Indian reservation territory. Wikipedia lists the Navajo Nation, the Fort Apache Indian Reservation and the Zuni Indian Reservation, and says reservation land makes up 68.34 percent of the county's area. Canyon de Chelly National Monument and part of Petrified Forest National Park are also inside the county, along with part of the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest.

At the 2020 census the county had 66,021 residents and 28,723 housing units, 23.0% of them vacant. Of occupied units, 73.2% were owner-occupied. School districts include St. Johns Unified, Round Valley Unified, Window Rock Unified, Chinle Unified and Ganado Unified. Interstate 40 and U.S. Routes 60, 160 and 191 cross the county.

Ask the County Assessor about any parcel on or near reservation land or on possessory rights land, since the Assessor's page counts improvements on possessory rights as real property.

faqs.q: Where is the Apache County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: The Recorder's office is at 75 West Cleveland in St. Johns, Arizona 85936, and is open 6:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through Thursday. The phone number is 928-337-7515.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Apache County?
faqs.a: State law sets most recording at $30 per instrument. Copies are $1 per page, plus $3 for the recorder's certificate and seal. Confirm current charges with the office before you mail a check.

faqs.q: Does an Apache County sale need an affidavit of property value?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the deed carries a listed exemption. Arizona law requires a complete affidavit signed by buyer and seller, or their agents, and the recorder must refuse a deed without one.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed of gift to a family member in Apache County?
faqs.a: A deed of gift is on the list of instruments exempt from the affidavit, and nominal-consideration transfers between close family members of residential property are also listed. The deed must note the specific exemption on its face.

faqs.q: Who releases a deed of trust in Apache County?
faqs.a: The Treasurer acts as public trustee and may release a deed of trust when the lender or holder asks. The release is then recorded with the County Recorder.
